target: Pixel geolocated VIIRS active-fire detections near the SNMF Barda de La Loma point and Bosque Tallado route during 2026-01-04 through 2026-01-10.

source.collection: NASA VIIRS Collection 2 VNP14IMG/VJ114IMG/VJ214IMG, 375 m L2 active-fire mask

qa_screen.source: NASA VIIRS Collection 2 Active Fire 375 m User Guide, Algorithm QA table.

spatial_test.route: Bosque Tallado desde la plataforma del Piltriquitron
spatial_test.route_distance_method: Local equirectangular point-to-segment distance on the reviewed route polyline; appropriate for this short route and 10 km neighborhood.
spatial_test.pixel_location_source: Sparse FP_latitude/FP_longitude arrays aligned with FP_line/FP_sample positions in the fire mask and algorithm QA grids.

limitations: This is a positive-detection screen. Absence of FP points does not establish that the route pixel was observed, clear, valid, or fire-free.
Full per-pixel geolocation is not included in the fire product. The sparse fire-pixel coordinates are sufficient to locate detections, but not clear-land pixels.
The SNMF incident has a reported start date but no exact ignition time; a same-day overpass cannot establish whether it occurred before or after the fire began.
A satellite detection is an algorithmic observation, not a field-confirmed ignition label; detections across sensors/passes may repeat one regional event.
This seven-day case study cannot estimate operational precision, recall, lead time, or calibration.
